sweep.anchor: termination/final disposition, whichever is later
sweep.ruleText: The statute says eligible records are to be expunged by October 1, 2027, or within 90 days after termination/final disposition, whichever is later. ("https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/sections/16-802")

sweep.anchor: the motion is granted
sweep.ruleText: The court may deny the motion on initial review, decide whether a hearing is needed, order a prosecutor response, or hold a hearing. If granted, the court must summarize the factual circumstances and rule as a matter of law that the person did not commit the offense or that no offense occurred. Eligible records must be expunged within 90 days after the motion is granted. ("https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/sections/16-803")

sweep.ruleText: A person released without conviction may file one year after the final disposition in the district where the charges originated. This route covers municipal ordinance violations, misdemeanors, felonies, certain Criminal Code or Motor Vehicle Code penalty assessments, and Motor Vehicle Code violations/deferred sentences. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-29/article-3a/section-29-3a-4/")

sweep.anchor: the conviction date, or two years after the arrest date if there was no conviction
sweep.ruleText: New Mexico has a special cannabis pathway. If a person was charged with an offense involving cannabis that is no longer a crime as of June 29, 2021, or would have resulted in a lesser offense under the Cannabis Regulation Act, public records relating to the arrest or conviction are automatically expunged two years after the conviction date, or two years after the arrest date if there was no conviction. For minors, the record is retained for two years or until the person turns 18, whichever comes first, and then automatically expunged. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-29/article-3a/section-29-3a-8/")

sweep.anchor: the ordinary court-record expungement
sweep.ruleText: DNA sample/profile expungement is separate from the ordinary court-record expungement. A person may request expungement of their DNA sample and DNA records from New Mexicos DNA identification system if the conviction that led to the sample was reversed, or if the arrest that led to the sample resulted in dismissal, nolle prosequi, successful pre-prosecution diversion, conditional discharge, misdemeanor conviction, acquittal, or did not result in a felony charge within one year. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-29/article-16/section-29-16-10/")

sweep.anchor: the state DNA identification system, the administrative center must ensure expungement from CODIS
sweep.ruleText: The person must provide a written request and certified documentation, such as a certified copy of the dismissal/nolle prosequi/diversion/conditional discharge/misdemeanor conviction/acquittal, or a sworn affidavit that no felony charges were filed within one year. If DNA records are expunged from the state DNA identification system, the administrative center must ensure expungement from CODIS. DNA expungement is not available if the person has a prior felony conviction or pending felony charge for which DNA collection is authorized. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/new-mexico/chapter-29/article-16/section-29-16-10/")

sweep.anchor: the date of acquittal if the statutory requirements are met
sweep.ruleText: If the person was acquitted of all charges based on the same conduct or criminal episode, Pennsylvania provides automatic expungement procedures. The statute does not apply to partial acquittals. The Commonwealth has 60 days to object, and expungement must occur no later than 12 months from the date of acquittal if the statutory requirements are met. ("https://www.legis.state.pa.us/WU01/LI/LI/CT/HTM/18/00.091..HTM")

A person may petition to expunge a summary offense conviction if they have been free of arrest or prosecution for five years following the conviction. Pennsylvania law states this summary-conviction expungement pathway is only for summary offenses. ("https://www.legis.state.pa.us/WU01/LI/LI/CT/HTM/18/00.091..HTM")

sweep.ruleText: A first offense conviction under South Carolinas fraudulent-check statute may be expunged after 1 year from conviction, but only if the conviction was a misdemeanor and the person had no other conviction during that one-year period. Felony fraudulent-check cases are not eligible under this route. This route is available only once. ("https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t34c011.php")

sweep.anchor: 3 years from the date of conviction, if they have no other convictions during that period
sweep.ruleText: A person convicted of a crime carrying a penalty of not more than 30 days imprisonment or a $1,000 fine may apply after 3 years from the date of conviction, if they have no other convictions during that period. This route does not apply to offenses involving operation of a motor vehicle. The statute also now includes certain first offense unlawful-possession-of-firearm-or-weapon convictions with a penalty of not more than 1 year or a $1,000 fine. ("https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t22c005.php")

sweep.anchor: conviction, with no other conviction during the period
sweep.ruleText: For third-degree domestic violence, the wait is 5 years from conviction, with no other conviction during the period. Conviction includes a guilty plea, nolo contendere plea, or bail forfeiture. Pending charges can block relief unless the pending charge is older than 5 years under the statutes tolling rules. This route is only available once. ("https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t22c005.php")

sweep.anchor: completing the sentence, including probation and parole, and then remaining conviction-free for 5 ye
sweep.ruleText: A person sentenced under the South Carolina Youthful Offender Act may apply after completing the sentence, including probation and parole, and then remaining conviction-free for 5 years. Closely connected offenses from the same incident may count as one offense. ("https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t22c005.php")

sweep.anchor: 3 years from completion of all sentence terms and conditions, if the person has no other conviction
sweep.ruleText: A first offense conviction under the eligible failure-to-stop provision may be expunged after 3 years from completion of all sentence terms and conditions, if the person has no other conviction during that 3-year period. This route does not apply to felony failure-to-stop cases. ("https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t56c005.php")

sweep.anchor: successful completion
sweep.ruleText: South Dakota has a special diversion path. A person who successfully completes a diversion program may be eligible for expungement of the entire criminal record related to the arrest if they are not charged with a new crime, other than petty offenses and minor traffic violations, within one year and thirty days after successful completion. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-23a/chapter-03/section-23a-3-35/")

If you completed a South Dakota diversion program and stayed clear of new charges for one year and thirty days, the States Attorney should file the dismissal and diversion-completion notice, and the court should grant expungement without a separate motion.

sweep.anchor: the public record after five years if all court-ordered conditions are satisfied and the person has
sweep.ruleText: South Dakota automatically removes certain minor cases from the public record after five years if all court-ordered conditions are satisfied and the person has no further convictions during that five-year period. This applies when the highest charged offense in the case was a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation, or Class 2 misdemeanor. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-23a/chapter-03/section-23a-3-34/")

sweep.anchor: public view after five years if the case was only a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation, or
sweep.ruleText: Some low-level South Dakota cases are removed from public view after five years if the case was only a petty offense, municipal ordinance violation, or Class 2 misdemeanor, all conditions were completed, and there were no new convictions. But the record may still be used by the court or to enhance later penalties.

sweep.anchor: one year, if the person completed treatment and all required conditions, the court must dismiss the
sweep.ruleText: South Dakota has a special deferred route for certain drug charges under SDCL 23A-27-53. For a guilty plea to specified controlled-substance offenses, the court may defer sentencing and require probation, treatment, testing, service, or other conditions. After one year, if the person completed treatment and all required conditions, the court must dismiss the original charge under the listed drug statutes when the person pleads guilty to the specified lesser offense. The statute also says the person is not eligible if there are aggravating circumstances or if the person is serving a sentence with the executive branch. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-23a/chapter-27/section-23a-27-53/")

sweep.anchor: penalties and disabilities resulting from the offense
sweep.ruleText: A South Dakota pardon through Chapter 24-14 releases the person from penalties and disabilities resulting from the offense. When the Governor grants a pardon under that chapter, the Governor orders official records relating to the arrest, charging document, trial, finding of guilt, pardon application, and Board of Pardons and Paroles proceedings sealed. A public document certifying the pardon remains filed with the Secretary of State for five years, then is sealed. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-24/chapter-14/section-24-14-11/")

sweep.anchor: one year has passed from the juveniles unconditional release from court jurisdiction or Department
sweep.ruleText: A juvenile, parent, guardian, or guardian ad litem may petition to seal juvenile delinquency records. The petition may be filed only after one year has passed from the juveniles unconditional release from court jurisdiction or Department of Corrections discharge, whichever is later. The court may seal records if the child has not been adjudicated delinquent since release/discharge, has no pending or instituted serious proceeding of the types listed in the statute, and the court finds rehabilitation has been attained. ("https://law.justia.com/codes/south-dakota/title-26/chapter-07a/section-26-7a-115/")
